mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Federal Funds rate above 4% for two consecutive months reduces the present value of expected equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4% and remains above for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: In the specified regime, the 60-day forward return is not statistically different from the 60-day historical average (p > 0.1) or the 20-day rolling IC exceeds 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly CPIAUCSL inflation rate exceeds 2% for three consecutive months, the market anticipates a faster than expected rate hike path, which elevates risk premia and drives negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: Over the trigger period, the 20-day forward return is positive and statistically significant (p < 0.05) or the IC is above 0.1 throughout the horizon.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in monthly PAYEMS (employment growth) above 200,000 jobs signals labor market strength that supports corporate earnings expectations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns within 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The 5-day forward return is negative or the 5-day IC is below -0.1, even after controlling for lagged employment data.

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of GDPC1 (goods orders) exceeds 1.5% above its 12-month trend, it indicates accelerating demand, which lowers financing costs and boosts equity valuations, yielding positive 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is not statistically positive (p > 0.1) or the IC remains below 0.05 during the trigger period.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in INDPRO (industrial production) of more than 5% suggests supply-side weakness that raises uncertainty and elevates volatility, producing negative S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward return is not significantly negative (p > 0.15) or the 60-day IC is above 0.1 during the contraction phase.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of FEDFUNDS below 1% and a rising HOUST (housing starts) series jointly indicate accommodative policy and rebuilding housing demand, which together drive positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 1% for 2 consecutive months AND HOUST rising
regime_hint: policy accommodation coupled with rebuilding construction
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is not positive or the interaction IC (Gaussian copula) exceeds 0.05 during the trigger window.

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE (unemployment rate) falls below 4% for two consecutive months in a recovery regime, it reduces labor market friction and supports corporate optimism, producing positive 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward return is not significantly positive (p > 0.1) or the 60-day IC is below 0.03 during the low-unemployment period.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in RSAFS (retail sales) of 10% or more indicates weakening consumer demand, which raises uncertainty and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is not negative or the 20-day IC is above 0.05 during the sales decline.
